links.text: BRM BC220 - Identity and Access Management

metadata.remarks:
Identity Authentication defines the capability to verify that an entity claiming an identity is the legitimate holder of that identity at the time of access. This capability establishes proof of identity but does not determine authorization or entitlements.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for roles and responsibilities, SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance activities related to authentication. ISCS controls are intentionally applied at the pattern level; internal components are descriptive only.

components.title: Authentication Events
components.description: Defines the generation and handling of authentication attempts and outcomes, including success, failure, and contextual metadata.

components.title: Authentication Context
components.description: Defines contextual factors used during authentication, such as device posture, location, time, and risk signals.

components.title: Step-Up Authentication
components.description: Defines mechanisms to dynamically increase authentication assurance in response to elevated risk or sensitivity.

components.title: Session Establishment
components.description: Defines the binding of successful authentication events to controlled, time-bounded sessions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Authentication policies and mechanisms must be defined and enforced. (NIST 800-171r3 IA-1)
Authentication mechanisms must resist replay, spoofing, and brute-force attacks. (NIST 800-171r3 IA-3)
Enhanced authentication and step-up mechanisms must be applied for high-risk access. (NIST 800-172r3 IA-7)
Authentication events must be logged for monitoring, audit, and incident response. (NIST 800-171r3 AU-2)
